newsitem.title: UK: Calls for probe into ex-BP minister rejected. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Calls for probe into ex-BP minister rejected. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]

text.p: Britain's Cabinet Secretary has rejected calls by the opposition Conservatives for an inquiry into a possible conflict of interest caused by the appointment of a former chairman of British Petroleum Co Plc as a minister.

Lord David Simon has retained his two million pounds worth of shares in BP despite being appointed Minister for Trade and Competitiveness in Europe, causing the Conservatives to question whether he could be impartial. (Corrects to make clear that Lord David Simon holds two millian pounds worth of shares as opposed to two million shares.)

But a Trade and Industry Department spokeswoman said Cabinet Secretary Sir Robin Butler had looked into the matter and rejected calls from Conservative Trade and Industry spokesman John Redwood for an inquiry.
"He is content with the arrangements for ensuring there is no conflict of interest," she said.
Redwood had complained that Simon had not included the shares on the House of Lords register of member's interests.

But Barbara Roche, another Trade and Industry Department minister, told BBC radio there was no requirement on Simon to do this, and that he had promised not to trade the shares before next January, when the position will be reviewed.
She said Simon was being kept away from government decisions which might impact on BP as a company. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
